This blog is about **qualitative comparative analysis (QCA)**, the **ThSQCA** R package, and practical tools for marketing research and data analysis. If you are new, here is a suggested order.

## If you are new to QCA

1. [Why QCA suits decision-making: looking for "recipes" instead of single effects](posts/why-qca-decisions/index.qmd)
2. [Is "good enough" the same goal as "loved"? A marketer's guide to threshold-sweep QCA](posts/qca-for-marketers/index.qmd)
3. [Papers and books for getting to know QCA: six to read first (basics)](posts/reading-list-basics/index.qmd)
4. [QCA in marketing and management: five papers to read first (applications)](posts/reading-list-applied/index.qmd)

## If you want to try threshold-sweep QCA in R

1. [Introducing ThSQCA: threshold-sweep QCA in R](posts/introducing-thsqca/index.qmd)
2. [ThSQCA for beginners, part 1: your first threshold sweep](posts/thsqca-beginners-1/index.qmd)
3. [Part 2: the four sweeps and how to choose a range](posts/thsqca-beginners-2/index.qmd)
4. [Part 3: solution types and multiple solutions](posts/thsqca-beginners-3/index.qmd)
5. [Part 4: reporting and checking your results](posts/thsqca-beginners-4/index.qmd)

## If you prefer to start from a tool

- [Tools](tools.qmd): browser-based tools for QCA and marketing research
- [Software](software.qmd): the ThSQCA package, with links to CRAN, GitHub, and the documentation
